title: Fix a Dangerous Python Script: Injection, Silent Failures, and No Timeout
intro: This script restarts a service over SSH and checks its health endpoint. It works, and a code review found four faults that each cause a real incident eventually: a shell command built by joining strings, a failed restart that goes unnoticed, an HTTP call that can hang for ever, and an exit code that always says success.

steps.prompt:
Fix restart_service.py:

(1) In restart(): replace os.system with subprocess.run, passing the command as a list
    ["ssh", host, "sudo", "systemctl", "restart", service]  and check=True.
    Import subprocess; remove the os import. Don't use shell=True.
(2) In healthy(): give requests.get a timeout (timeout=5).
(3) In healthy(): replace the bare 'except:' with 'except requests.RequestException:'.
(4) In main(): when the service is unhealthy, exit with status 1 using sys.exit(1).
steps.fake_output:
$ python restart_service.py web-1 shop https://web-1.internal/health
unhealthy
$ echo $?
1
steps.explanation: The same behaviour when everything works, and an honest failure when it doesn't.
steps.why: The four faults in turn. (1) os.system with joined strings hands a line to a shell. If 'service' ever comes from a ticket, a form, or a file, a value like 'nginx; rm -rf /' runs both commands. A list passed to subprocess.run goes to the program as separate arguments, with no shell to interpret anything. os.system also discards the result; check=True raises CalledProcessError if ssh or systemctl fails, so the script stops instead of going on to 'check health' of a service it never restarted. (2) requests has no timeout by default: one unresponsive host and this script, and the pipeline running it, hang indefinitely. Every network call needs one. (3) A bare 'except:' catches everything, including KeyboardInterrupt and the NameError from a typo in your own code, and turns them all into 'False'. Catch the specific exception you expect. (4) Printing 'unhealthy' and exiting 0 tells the calling pipeline the restart succeeded. Ruff flags three of these automatically (S605, S113, E722), which is the argument for running a linter on automation code (scripting-tutorial-003).
